articles.title: Will We Ever Have Another Conor McGregor? #ufc
articles.description: Will the UFC ever have another Conor McGregor? Chael Sonnen has a definitive answer: **No.** Chael explains why Conor McGregor was truly one of one — not just because of his ability to fight, but because he mastered every part of being a superstar. The fame, the entertainment, the professionalism, the personality, and the ability to turn every moment into an event made Conor something the sport may never see again. But Chael also points out something fans often overlook when a massive star leaves the sport: **the fans don't disappear.** They simply move on and find someone else to support. The UFC will always have new stars. The real challenge is finding the one athlete capable of capturing the attention of an entire generation and bringing all those fans along for the ride. Conor McGregor did exactly that. There will never be another Conor. But Chael believes there will be another superstar — and he's looking forward to seeing who becomes the next one. #ConorMcGregor #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCStars #MMAHistory #UFCNews #CombatSports

articles.title: Arman vs Oliveira but what about with Gaethje? #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan vs. Charles Oliveira for the BMF title could be the perfect solution for the UFC's lightweight division — and Chael Sonnen explains why. Chael believes Arman is a legitimate number-one contender, but with the BMF title sitting right there at lightweight, a matchup with Oliveira suddenly makes too much sense. It gives Arman a massive fight while taking another contender off the board and completely reshaping what's next for Justin Gaethje. So who does Gaethje fight next? A rematch with Paddy Pimblett doesn't seem likely. Ilia Topuria may not be ready to jump right back into another title fight. A Max Holloway rematch is possible, but Gaethje has reportedly expressed interest in something new. Chael believes the lightweight division may ultimately come down to Paddy or Ilia trying to take the belt from Gaethje — and one of them could be the final opponent of Gaethje's career. The question is simple: **Which fighter is best equipped to take the title from Justin Gaethje?** #ArmanTsarukyan #CharlesOliveira #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #BMF #PaddyPimblett #IliaTopuria #UFCAnalysis

articles.title: 20 Years Ago Today, The WEC Named A Card After Our Founder 🔥🔥
articles.description: Twenty years ago today, the WEC named a card after a man who never fought a day in his life. He founded this site. Ryan Bennett co-founded MMAWeekly.com. Before Zuffa bought the WEC, he was its play-by-play voice. He was the guy holding the microphone in the cage after UFC 33 through 40. And every day he hosted MMAWeekly Radio alongside Frank Trigg. If you followed this sport in the early 2000s, you heard Ryan whether you knew his name or not. On May 31, 2006, he was driving his family across Utah on I-15. The vehicle went off the road. His wife and all four of his children survived. Ryan was killed instantly. He was 35. Two months later the WEC put his name on the card — WEC 22, July 28, 2006. Wes Sims was offered a bigger payday somewhere else that same weekend. He turned it down. In his own words in this video: "You can't put a price tag on friendship." Then he opened the fight with a flying drop kick — because that was the one thing Ryan had asked him for, over and over, for years. He finished it in 28 seconds. And on that same card, a young Brazilian named Glover Teixeira choked his opponent out in under 90 seconds. Fifteen years later he'd be UFC light heavyweight champion of the world. One night in a casino ballroom in Lemoore, California, for the guy who spent his whole life pointing a microphone at everybody else. If you remember Ryan, tell us below. 🤍 #RyanBennett Website: http://www.MMAWeekly.com/ Subscribe on Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/subscription_center?add_user=MMAWeeklyVideos Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/MMAWeeklycom-176775391774/ Twitter: https://twitter.com/MMAWeeklycom/ Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/mmaweekly/

articles.title: THIS DAY in MMA - JULY 27 🔥
articles.description: THIS DAY in MMA - JULY 27 🔥 2024 — Belal Muhammad walks into Leon Edwards' hometown of Manchester and takes his welterweight title. Nine takedowns in front of 17,000 people who came to boo him. 2019 — Cris Cyborg beats Felicia Spencer at UFC 240. Nobody in that building knew they'd just watched her last fight in the UFC. Six days later she was released. 2013 — Demetrious Johnson armbars John Moraga with 77 seconds left in the fifth round. His first ever finish in the Octagon, and the latest finish in UFC history at the time. 1997 — Mark Kerr makes his UFC debut at UFC 14 and wins the entire heavyweight tournament in ONE night. They called him The Smashing Machine. Almost 30 years later, Dwayne Johnson played him on screen. Same date. articles.title: Are They Going To Give Conor Another Chance? #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is challenging the way fans remember Conor McGregor's biggest losses. According to Chael, Conor has rarely been in a fight where he was simply overwhelmed from start to finish. Even against Khabib Nurmagomedov, Chael argues that there were moments of resistance and competitive exchanges that fans often overlook. The Dustin Poirier rematch was different. That fight played out largely on the feet, in the exact area where Conor wanted to compete — and Poirier overwhelmed him. But then there's Nate Diaz. Chael believes Diaz is the one opponent who truly beat Conor in a way that stands out, and now he's taking another look at Conor's history with Max Holloway. Conor fought Max twice and came away with mixed results — but Chael points out that Conor was dealing with a significant leg issue in both fights. Is that just Chael entering "Spin City," or is there something about the matchup that deserves another look? If Conor gets another opportunity against Max, Chael believes we'll have to reconsider everything we thought we knew about their first fight. #ConorMcGregor #MaxHolloway #NateDiaz #Khabib #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCAnalysis

articles.title: Can Ian Garry Beat Islam Makhachev? #ufc
articles.description: Can Ian Machado Garry really beat Islam Makhachev? Chael Sonnen believes the answer is yes — and he thinks Garry has a specific path to victory. Garry has already made his confidence clear, promising to use his size, speed, length, and striking to take Islam's title and throne. But Chael explains why this matchup is far more complicated than simply picking the bigger fighter. Ian Garry's biggest weapon could be his ability to control distance. If he can consistently keep Islam at the end of his punches, he may be able to force the champion to fight at a range he's not comfortable with. But there's a major tradeoff. Chael points out that Islam is an elite wrestler, and Garry's height and length could actually give Islam more opportunities to grab and control him. The question becomes whether Garry can use his physical advantages to stay out of Islam's world — or whether Islam can close the distance and bring the fight to his. After Garry's performance against Shavkat Rakhmonov, Chael believes we've already seen evidence that his wrestling can be challenged. Now, Garry has the chance to prove just how good he really is. #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCAnalysis #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Ring Rust Or Father Time? #ufc
articles.description: Can Conor McGregor actually turn things around against Max Holloway? Chael Sonnen believes it's possible — but only under the right circumstances. Chael points back to Conor's rematch with Nate Diaz, explaining how the first loss forced McGregor to make a promise to himself: no matter how tired he became or how much punishment he took, he was going to fight for all 25 minutes. But beating Max Holloway is a completely different challenge. Chael questions whether Conor's performance was the result of ring rust or simply father time catching up with him. After a long layoff, Max could be back in the gym immediately while Conor could potentially be forced to spend months recovering before even beginning another training camp. That creates a massive gap. Still, Chael believes a rematch could become a real conversation if Conor had an extended period to prepare and rebuild. The timeline matters, the weight class matters, and most importantly, Conor would have to prove that what we saw was not the final version of him. The first step? Getting healthy. Then, maybe, the conversation about Max can begin. #ConorMcGregor #MaxHolloway #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCAnalysis #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Paddy Just Made a Brilliant Investment #ufc
articles.description: Paddy Pimblett may have just made one of the smartest investments in MMA — and Chael Sonnen thinks the $13,000 stool he bought could become far more valuable over time. Chael breaks down why Paddy's custom piece of art is completely different from an ordinary chair. It isn't just furniture. It's a unique collectible with a story attached to one of the UFC's biggest personalities. And Chael takes the idea even further. What happens if Paddy brings the stool to a future fight? According to Chael, Paddy wouldn't need a massive crowd to make the investment back — and the marketing potential could be enormous. This is the kind of unconventional thinking that turns a simple piece of artwork into a memorable part of a fighter's brand.
